description: CEE question bank after intra-set and inter-set deduplication.

questions.text: Which theory of origin of life was experimentally supported by Miller and Urey?
questions.rationale: Miller-Urey experiment supported the Oparin-Haldane theory of chemical evolution.

questions.text: Which of the following is a paleontological evidence of evolution?
questions.rationale: Fossils provide direct paleontological evidence of evolution.

questions.text: The theory of natural selection was proposed by:
questions.rationale: Darwin proposed natural selection in his theory of evolution.

questions.text: Which human ancestor is considered the earliest hominid in the line to modern man?
questions.rationale: Ramapithecus is regarded as the earliest hominid ancestor.

questions.text: Lamarck's theory of evolution is based primarily on:
questions.rationale: Lamarckism emphasizes inheritance of acquired characteristics.

questions.text: Which type of evidence shows that the forelimbs of a bat, whale and human share a common origin?
questions.rationale: Homologous organs share a common embryonic origin despite different functions.

questions.text: Which phylum includes animals with a notochord at some stage of life?
questions.rationale: Chordates possess a notochord at some stage of their life cycle.

questions.text: Which class of vertebrates has a three-chambered heart?
questions.rationale: Amphibians have a three-chambered heart (two atria, one ventricle).

questions.text: Which phylum is characterized by jointed appendages?
questions.rationale: Arthropods have jointed appendages and an exoskeleton.

questions.text: Which class do butterflies and beetles belong to?
questions.rationale: Butterflies and beetles are insects of class Insecta.

questions.text: Which phylum includes animals with a mantle and a muscular foot?
questions.rationale: Molluscs have a mantle and a muscular foot.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of mammals?
questions.rationale: Mammals are characterized by mammary glands and hair.

questions.text: Which tissue lines the inner surface of blood vessels?
questions.rationale: Simple squamous epithelium (endothelium) lines blood vessels.

questions.text: Which connective tissue stores fat and provides insulation?
questions.rationale: Adipose tissue stores fat and insulates the body.

questions.text: Which muscle tissue is voluntary and striated?
questions.rationale: Skeletal muscle is voluntary and shows striations.

questions.text: Which tissue transmits nerve impulses?
questions.rationale: Nervous tissue conducts impulses via neurons.

questions.text: Which type of epithelium is best suited for diffusion and filtration?
questions.rationale: Simple squamous epithelium is thin, ideal for diffusion and filtration.

questions.text: Which tissue connects bone to bone at a joint?
questions.rationale: Ligaments connect bone to bone; tendons connect muscle to bone.

questions.text: Which disease is caused by Plasmodium?
questions.rationale: Plasmodium is the protozoan that causes malaria.

questions.text: Which mosquito genus transmits malaria?
questions.rationale: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium.

questions.text: How many pairs of aortic arches (hearts) does an earthworm have?
questions.rationale: Earthworms have 5 pairs of aortic arches acting as hearts.

questions.text: Which respiratory pigment is present in the blood of an earthworm?
questions.rationale: Earthworm blood contains dissolved hemoglobin.

questions.text: Which structure in the frog is used for respiration on land?
questions.rationale: Adult frogs respire through lungs and skin on land.

questions.text: In the life cycle of Plasmodium, which stage is infective to humans?
questions.rationale: Sporozoites injected by mosquito bite are infective to humans.

questions.text: Which organ of the earthworm is responsible for excretion?
questions.rationale: Earthworms excrete through nephridia.

questions.text: Which type of malaria is caused by Plasmodium falciparum?
questions.rationale: P. falciparum causes malignant tertian malaria, the most severe form.

questions.text: Which enzyme in saliva digests starch?
questions.rationale: Salivary amylase hydrolyzes starch into maltose.

questions.text: Which organ produces bile?
questions.rationale: The liver produces bile, stored in the gallbladder.

questions.text: Where does most nutrient absorption occur?
questions.rationale: The small intestine with villi absorbs most nutrients.

questions.text: Which structure filters blood in the kidney?
questions.rationale: The glomerulus filters blood during urine formation.

questions.text: Which hormone lowers blood glucose level?
questions.rationale: Insulin lowers blood glucose by promoting cellular uptake.

questions.text: Which chamber of the heart pumps blood to the lungs?
questions.rationale: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs.

questions.text: Which blood group is the universal donor?
questions.rationale: O negative lacks A, B and Rh antigens, so it can be given to all.

questions.text: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?
questions.rationale: The cerebellum coordinates balance and voluntary movements.

questions.text: Which hormone regulates blood calcium level?
questions.rationale: PTH from parathyroid glands raises blood calcium.

questions.text: Which structure in the eye focuses light on the retina?
questions.rationale: The lens focuses light onto the retina.

questions.text: Which part of the ear is responsible for balance?
questions.rationale: Semicircular canals detect rotational movement for balance.

questions.text: Which blood cells produce antibodies?
questions.rationale: B lymphocytes differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies.

questions.text: Which gas is exchanged in the alveoli of the lungs?
questions.rationale: Alveoli exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide by diffusion.

questions.text: Which hormone stimulates milk production in the mammary glands?
questions.rationale: Prolactin stimulates milk synthesis in mammary glands.

questions.text: Which process forms gametes in the gonads?
questions.rationale: Gametogenesis is the formation of gametes (sperm and ova).

questions.text: Which vitamin is synthesized in the skin on exposure to sunlight?
questions.rationale: UV light converts 7-dehydrocholesterol to vitamin D3.

questions.text: Which structure connects the two cerebral hemispheres?
questions.rationale: The corpus callosum connects the cerebral hemispheres.

questions.text: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.rationale: The pulmonary vein is the only vein carrying oxygenated blood.

questions.text: Which bacterium causes tuberculosis?
questions.rationale: Mycobacterium tuberculosis causes TB.

questions.text: Which virus causes Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS)?
questions.rationale: HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) causes AIDS.

questions.text: Which type of immunity is present from birth?
questions.rationale: Innate immunity is present from birth and is non-specific.

questions.text: Which type of vaccine uses a weakened form of the pathogen?
questions.rationale: Live attenuated vaccines use weakened live pathogens.

questions.text: Which organism causes cholera?
questions.rationale: Vibrio cholerae causes cholera, a severe diarrheal disease.

questions.text: Antibodies are produced by which type of cells?
questions.rationale: Plasma cells (from B lymphocytes) produce antibodies.

questions.text: Which technique is used to detect genetic abnormalities in the fetus by examining amniotic fluid?
questions.rationale: Amniocentesis analyzes amniotic fluid for fetal genetic disorders.

questions.text: Which process involves fertilization of an egg outside the body?
questions.rationale: IVF fertilizes the egg outside the body in a laboratory.

questions.text: Which microorganism is used in the production of yogurt?
questions.rationale: Lactobacillus ferments milk to produce yogurt.

questions.text: Which gas is the major contributor to the greenhouse effect?
questions.rationale: CO2 is a major greenhouse gas trapping heat.

questions.text: Which category in the IUCN Red List indicates a species at very high risk of extinction?
questions.rationale: Critically Endangered is the highest risk category before extinction.

questions.text: Which type of adaptation allows birds to fly?
questions.rationale: Volant adaptation enables flight in birds.

questions.text: Which wetland site in Nepal is designated as a Ramsar site?
questions.rationale: Koshi Tappu Wildlife Reserve is a Ramsar site in Nepal.

questions.text: Which monosaccharide is the main energy source for cells?
questions.rationale: Glucose is the primary energy source for cellular respiration.

questions.text: Which biomolecule acts as a biological catalyst?
questions.rationale: Enzymes are proteins that catalyze biochemical reactions.

questions.text: Which lipid is a major component of the cell membrane?
questions.rationale: Phospholipids form the bilayer of cell membranes.

questions.text: Which mineral is a component of chlorophyll?
questions.rationale: Magnesium is at the center of the chlorophyll molecule.

questions.text: Which plant group is known as the amphibians of the plant kingdom?
questions.rationale: Bryophytes need water for reproduction, like amphibians.

questions.text: Which plant group includes ferns?
questions.rationale: Ferns belong to Pteridophyta, the first vascular plants.

questions.text: Which plant group produces naked seeds without flowers?
questions.rationale: Gymnosperms produce naked seeds without flowers or fruits.

questions.text: Which plant group includes flowering plants?
questions.rationale: Angiosperms are flowering plants with enclosed seeds.

questions.text: Which family of flowering plants has the floral formula with 5 sepals, 5 petals and 5 stamens?
questions.rationale: Solanaceae typically has 5 sepals, 5 petals and 5 stamens.

questions.text: Which medicinal plant is known as Sarpagandha and used for hypertension?
questions.rationale: Rauwolfia serpentina (Sarpagandha) is used to treat hypertension.

questions.text: Which plant is known as Yarsagumba and is a valuable medicinal fungus in Nepal?
questions.rationale: Ophiocordyceps sinensis (Yarsagumba) is a prized medicinal fungus.

questions.text: Which plant is commonly known as Neem and has antibacterial properties?
questions.rationale: Azadirachta indica (Neem) has antibacterial and medicinal properties.

questions.text: Which group of algae is characterized by the presence of chlorophyll a and b and is green?
questions.rationale: Chlorophyceae (green algae) contain chlorophyll a and b.

questions.text: Which structure of Spirogyra is used for sexual reproduction?
questions.rationale: Spirogyra reproduces sexually by conjugation through a conjugation tube.

questions.text: Which plant group includes liverworts?
questions.rationale: Liverworts belong to Hepaticopsida.

questions.text: Which family of plants is characterized by papilionaceous corolla?
questions.rationale: Fabaceae (legumes) have a papilionaceous (butterfly-shaped) corolla.

questions.text: Which biogeochemical cycle involves the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into usable forms?
questions.rationale: The nitrogen cycle converts atmospheric N2 into usable forms via fixation.

questions.text: Which phenomenon is caused by the depletion of the ozone layer?
questions.rationale: Ozone depletion allows more harmful UV radiation to reach Earth.

questions.text: Which type of ecological succession begins on bare rock?
questions.rationale: Xerosere is succession starting on dry or bare rock surfaces.

questions.text: Which forest type is found in the Terai region of Nepal?
questions.rationale: Tropical deciduous forests dominate the Terai region.

questions.text: Which gas is primarily responsible for acid rain?
questions.rationale: SO2 and NOx dissolve in rainwater to form acid rain.

questions.text: Which process describes the gradual change in species composition of an ecosystem over time?
questions.rationale: Ecological succession is the gradual change in community composition.

questions.text: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.rationale: Mitochondria produce ATP through cellular respiration.

questions.text: Which organelle contains chlorophyll and performs photosynthesis?
questions.rationale: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll for photosynthesis.

questions.text: Which organelle is responsible for protein synthesis?
questions.rationale: Ribosomes synthesize proteins from mRNA.

questions.text: Which type of cell division reduces the chromosome number by half?
questions.rationale: Meiosis produces haploid gametes with half the chromosome number.

questions.text: Which structure controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell?
questions.rationale: The cell membrane is selectively permeable and controls transport.

questions.text: Which organelle is involved in the synthesis and packaging of proteins and lipids?
questions.rationale: The Golgi body modifies, sorts and packages proteins and lipids.

questions.text: Which phase of the cell cycle is the longest and involves cell growth?
questions.rationale: Interphase is the longest phase involving growth and DNA replication.

questions.text: Who is known as the father of genetics?
questions.rationale: Mendel established the laws of inheritance through pea plant experiments.

questions.text: Which molecule carries the genetic information in most organisms?
questions.rationale: DNA carries hereditary genetic information.

questions.text: Which process copies DNA before cell division?
questions.rationale: DNA replication duplicates the genome before division.

questions.text: Which genetic disorder is caused by trisomy of chromosome 21?
questions.rationale: Down's syndrome results from trisomy 21.

questions.text: Which type of inheritance is shown by color blindness in humans?
questions.rationale: Color blindness is an X-linked (sex-linked) recessive trait.

questions.text: Which genetic disorder is characterized by the absence of one X chromosome in females?
questions.rationale: Turner's syndrome (45, X) results from a missing X chromosome.

questions.text: Which phenomenon explains the exchange of segments between homologous chromosomes?
questions.rationale: Crossing over exchanges segments between homologous chromosomes during meiosis.

questions.text: Which genetic disorder is caused by trisomy of chromosome 18?
questions.rationale: Edward's syndrome results from trisomy 18.

questions.text: Which tissue transports water and minerals upward in plants?
questions.rationale: Xylem conducts water and minerals from roots to leaves.

questions.text: Which tissue transports food (sugars) in plants?
questions.rationale: Phloem transports sugars from source to sink.

questions.text: Which type of vascular bundle has xylem and phloem on the same radius?
questions.rationale: Conjoint bundles have xylem and phloem on the same radius.

questions.text: Which tissue provides mechanical support and is composed of dead cells?
questions.rationale: Sclerenchyma consists of dead cells providing mechanical support.

questions.text: In a dicot stem, the vascular bundles are arranged in which pattern?
questions.rationale: Dicot stems have vascular bundles arranged in a ring.

questions.text: Which process converts light energy into chemical energy in plants?
questions.rationale: Photosynthesis stores light energy as chemical energy in glucose.

questions.text: Which gas is released as a by-product of photosynthesis?
questions.rationale: Oxygen is released during the light reactions of photosynthesis.

questions.text: Which process is the loss of water vapor from plant leaves?
questions.rationale: Transpiration is water loss through stomata.

questions.text: Which hormone promotes cell elongation and apical dominance?
questions.rationale: Auxin promotes cell elongation and apical dominance.

questions.text: Which hormone promotes fruit ripening?
questions.rationale: Ethylene promotes fruit ripening.

questions.text: Which pathway fixes CO2 in C4 plants?
questions.rationale: C4 plants use the Hatch-Slack pathway for CO2 fixation.

questions.text: Which process breaks down glucose to release energy in plants?
questions.rationale: Respiration breaks down glucose to release ATP.

questions.text: Which hormone induces seed dormancy?
questions.rationale: Abscisic acid (ABA) induces and maintains seed dormancy.

questions.text: Which process is the movement of water across a semipermeable membrane?
questions.rationale: Osmosis is the movement of water across a semipermeable membrane.

questions.text: Which process is the transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma?
questions.rationale: Pollination transfers pollen from anther to stigma.

questions.text: Which structure develops into the seed after fertilization?
questions.rationale: The ovule develops into the seed after fertilization.

questions.text: Which type of endosperm is formed by the fusion of one sperm with two polar nuclei?
questions.rationale: Double fertilization produces triploid (3n) endosperm.

questions.text: Which type of pollination occurs within the same flower?
questions.rationale: Self-pollination transfers pollen within the same flower.

questions.text: Which technique grows plant cells or tissues in a sterile nutrient medium?
questions.rationale: Plant tissue culture grows plant tissues in sterile media.

questions.text: Which organism is used as a biofertilizer to fix atmospheric nitrogen?
questions.rationale: Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen in legume root nodules.

questions.text: Which crop is a major cash crop of Nepal?
questions.rationale: Tea is a major cash crop grown in Nepal.

questions.text: Which process involves the manipulation of an organism's genes using biotechnology?
questions.rationale: Genetic engineering manipulates genes using biotechnology.

questions.text: Which plant is a major source of natural rubber?
questions.rationale: Natural rubber is tapped from Hevea brasiliensis.

questions.text: What is the pH of a neutral solution at 25°C?
questions.rationale: Pure water has a pH of 7 at 25°C.

questions.text: Which gas law states that pressure is inversely proportional to volume at constant temperature?
questions.rationale: Boyle's law: P ∝ 1/V at constant temperature.

questions.text: What is the unit of molarity?
questions.rationale: Molarity is moles of solute per liter of solution (mol/L).

questions.text: What is the oxidation state of oxygen in hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)?
questions.rationale: Oxygen has an oxidation state of -1 in peroxides.

questions.text: Which process absorbs heat from the surroundings?
questions.rationale: Endothermic processes absorb heat.

questions.text: What is Avogadro's number?
questions.rationale: Avogadro's number is 6.022 × 10^23 particles per mole.

questions.text: What is the normality of a 1 M solution of H2SO4?
questions.rationale: H2SO4 has 2 replaceable H+ ions, so 1 M = 2 N.

questions.text: What is the pH of a 0.001 M HCl solution?
Which law states that the rate of a reaction is proportional to the product of concentrations of reactants?
questions.rationale: The law of mass action relates reaction rate to reactant concentrations.

questions.text: Which principle states that a system at equilibrium responds to stress by shifting to counteract it?
questions.rationale: Le Chatelier's principle describes equilibrium shifts under stress.

questions.text: Which quantum number describes the shape of an orbital?
questions.rationale: The azimuthal quantum number (l) determines orbital shape.

questions.text: Which principle states that no two electrons in an atom can have the same set of four quantum numbers?
questions.rationale: Pauli's exclusion principle governs electron configuration.

questions.text: Which type of bond is formed by the sharing of electrons between atoms?
questions.rationale: Covalent bonds form by electron sharing.

questions.text: Which theory explains the shape of molecules based on electron pair repulsion?
questions.rationale: VSEPR theory predicts molecular shape from electron pair repulsion.

questions.text: What is the relationship between Kp and Kc for a gaseous reaction?
questions.rationale: Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn where Δn is the change in moles of gas.

questions.text: Which law states that the total pressure of a gas mixture is the sum of partial pressures?
questions.rationale: Dalton's law of partial pressures applies to gas mixtures.

questions.text: Which type of reaction has a half-life independent of initial concentration?
questions.rationale: First-order reactions have a constant half-life.

questions.text: Which cell converts chemical energy into electrical energy?
questions.rationale: A galvanic (voltaic) cell converts chemical to electrical energy.

questions.text: Which quantity is a measure of the disorder of a system?
questions.rationale: Entropy measures the disorder or randomness of a system.

questions.text: Which process is the direct conversion of a solid to a gas?
questions.rationale: Sublimation is the direct solid-to-gas transition.

questions.text: Which element has the atomic number 6?
questions.rationale: Carbon has atomic number 6.

questions.text: Which group of the periodic table contains the noble gases?
questions.rationale: Noble gases are in Group 18.

questions.text: Which is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust?
questions.rationale: Oxygen makes up about 46% of the Earth's crust.

questions.text: Which element is a halogen?
questions.rationale: Chlorine is a halogen in Group 17.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula of common salt?
questions.rationale: Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl.

questions.text: Which element is a transition metal?
questions.rationale: Iron is a transition metal in the 3d series.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula of limestone?
questions.rationale: Limestone is calcium carbonate, CaCO3.

questions.text: Which element has the chemical symbol K?
questions.rationale: K is the symbol for potassium.

questions.text: Which is the most electronegative element?
questions.rationale: Fluorine is the most electronegative element.

questions.text: Which gas is used in the Haber process to produce ammonia?
questions.rationale: The Haber process combines N2 and H2 to make NH3.

questions.text: Which compound is used in bleaching powder?
questions.rationale: Bleaching powder contains calcium hypochlorite, Ca(OCl)Cl.

questions.text: Which acid is found in vinegar?
questions.rationale: Vinegar contains acetic acid.

questions.text: Which element is a metalloid?
questions.rationale: Silicon is a metalloid with properties of metals and non-metals.

questions.text: Which process is used to extract metals from their ores?
questions.rationale: Metallurgy is the extraction of metals from ores.

questions.text: Which functional group is present in alcohols?
questions.rationale: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl group (-OH).

questions.text: What is the general formula of alkanes?
questions.rationale: Alkanes have the general formula CnH2n+2.

questions.text: What is the simplest alkane?
questions.rationale: Methane (CH4) is the simplest alkane.

questions.text: Which functional group is present in carboxylic acids?
questions.rationale: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl group (-COOH).

questions.text: What are the products of complete combustion of methane?
questions.rationale: Complete combustion of methane yields CO2 and H2O.

questions.text: Which functional group is present in aldehydes?
questions.rationale: Aldehydes contain the formyl group (-CHO).

questions.text: What is the general formula of alkenes?
questions.rationale: Alkenes with one double bond have formula CnH2n.

questions.text: Which functional group is present in ketones?
questions.rationale: Ketones contain the carbonyl group (-CO-) within the chain.

questions.text: Which compound is a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.rationale: Methane has only single C-H bonds and is saturated.

questions.text: What is the IUPAC name of CH3CH2OH?
questions.rationale: CH3CH2OH is a two-carbon alcohol, ethanol.

questions.text: Which compound is an aromatic hydrocarbon?
questions.rationale: Benzene has a stable aromatic ring.

questions.text: Which type of reaction is the addition of H2 to ethene?
questions.rationale: Adding H2 to ethene is hydrogenation, producing ethane.

questions.text: Which reagent is used to test for aldehydes?
questions.rationale: Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) tests for aldehydes.

questions.text: Which type of bond joins amino acids in proteins?
questions.rationale: Peptide bonds link amino acids in proteins.

questions.text: What is the main product of alcoholic fermentation by yeast?
questions.rationale: Yeast ferments sugars to produce ethanol and CO2.

questions.text: Which compound is an isomer of butane?
questions.rationale: Isobutane has the same formula C4H10 as butane.

questions.text: Which type of reaction is esterification?
questions.rationale: Esterification is a condensation reaction between an acid and alcohol.

questions.text: Which compound is a polymer?
questions.rationale: Polyethylene is a polymer of ethene monomers.

questions.text: Which type of mechanism involves a two-step process with a carbocation intermediate?
questions.rationale: SN1 proceeds via a carbocation intermediate in two steps.

questions.text: Which compound is used as a general anesthetic?
questions.rationale: Diethyl ether was historically used as a general anesthetic.

questions.text: Which process is used for the industrial manufacture of ammonia?
questions.rationale: Ammonia is manufactured by the Haber process.

questions.text: Which process is used to manufacture sulphuric acid industrially?
questions.rationale: Sulphuric acid is made by the Contact process.

questions.text: Which process is used to manufacture nitric acid?
questions.rationale: Nitric acid is manufactured by the Ostwald process.

questions.text: Which compound is used as a fertilizer to supply nitrogen to plants?
questions.rationale: Urea (CO(NH2)2) is a nitrogen-rich fertilizer.

questions.text: Which type of material is used to make biodegradable plastics?
questions.rationale: Polylactic acid (PLA) is a biodegradable polymer.

questions.text: Which technique separates components based on their differential migration on a stationary phase?
questions.rationale: Paper chromatography separates components by differential migration.

questions.text: Which test is used to detect nitrogen, sulphur and halogens in organic compounds?
questions.rationale: Lassaigne's test detects hetero-elements in organic compounds.

questions.text: Which type of titration involves the use of potassium permanganate?
questions.rationale: Permanganometric titration uses KMnO4 as the oxidizing agent.

questions.text: Which technique separates a mixture based on differences in boiling points?
questions.rationale: Distillation separates components by boiling point differences.

questions.text: Which indicator is commonly used in acid-base titration?
questions.rationale: Phenolphthalein and methyl orange are common acid-base indicators.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.rationale: Force is measured in newtons (N).

questions.text: What is the approximate acceleration due to gravity on Earth?
questions.rationale: g ≈ 9.8 m/s² on Earth.

questions.text: Which law states that force equals mass times acceleration?
questions.rationale: F = ma is Newton's second law.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of work?
questions.rationale: Work and energy are measured in joules (J).

questions.text: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.rationale: Velocity has both magnitude and direction.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.rationale: Power is measured in watts (W).

questions.text: Which of the following is a non-contact force?
questions.rationale: Gravity acts at a distance without contact.

questions.text: A body moving in a circle at constant speed has:
questions.rationale: Direction changes continuously, so velocity changes.

questions.text: What is the momentum of a 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s?
questions.rationale: Momentum p = mv = 2 × 3 = 6 kg·m/s.

questions.text: Which quantity is the rate of change of displacement?
questions.rationale: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement.

questions.text: What is the kinetic energy of a 4 kg object moving at 5 m/s?
questions.rationale: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 4 × 25 = 50 J.

questions.text: Which principle states that the total momentum of an isolated system is conserved?
questions.rationale: Momentum is conserved in an isolated system.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of temperature?
questions.rationale: Kelvin (K) is the SI unit of temperature.

questions.text: Which mode of heat transfer occurs through direct contact?
questions.rationale: Conduction transfers heat through direct contact.

questions.text: Which law states that energy cannot be created or destroyed?
questions.rationale: The first law is the conservation of energy.

questions.text: Which mode of heat transfer occurs through fluid movement?
questions.rationale: Convection transfers heat through fluid movement.

questions.text: Which process transfers heat through empty space?
questions.rationale: Radiation needs no medium for heat transfer.

questions.text: Which device measures atmospheric pressure?
questions.rationale: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.text: What is the specific heat capacity of water?
questions.rationale: Water has a high specific heat of 4.18 J/g°C.

questions.text: Which process is isothermal?
questions.rationale: Isothermal means constant temperature.

questions.text: Which law relates to the entropy of an isolated system?
questions.rationale: The second law states entropy of an isolated system increases.

questions.text: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
questions.rationale: Light travels at 3 × 10^8 m/s in vacuum.

questions.text: Which type of wave requires a medium to travel?
questions.rationale: Sound is a mechanical wave requiring a medium.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of frequency?
questions.rationale: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz).

questions.text: Which lens converges light rays?
questions.rationale: A convex lens converges light rays.

questions.text: Which phenomenon explains the formation of a rainbow?
questions.rationale: Dispersion splits white light into colors.

questions.text: Which type of mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image?
questions.rationale: Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, diminished images.

questions.text: Which lens is used to correct myopia (nearsightedness)?
questions.rationale: Concave lenses diverge light to correct myopia.

questions.text: What is the speed of sound in air at room temperature?
questions.rationale: Sound travels at about 343 m/s in air.

questions.text: Which phenomenon is the bending of light around obstacles?
questions.rationale: Diffraction is the bending of waves around obstacles.

questions.text: Which law states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection?
questions.rationale: The law of reflection states i = r.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.rationale: Electric current is measured in amperes (A).

questions.text: Which law is expressed as V = IR?
questions.rationale: Ohm's law relates voltage, current and resistance.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of resistance?
questions.rationale: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω).

questions.text: Which material is a good electrical conductor?
questions.rationale: Copper is a metal and conducts electricity well.

questions.text: What is the total resistance of two 6 Ω resistors connected in parallel?
What is the SI unit of magnetic field strength?
questions.rationale: Magnetic field strength is measured in teslas (T).

questions.text: Which device converts electrical energy into mechanical energy?
questions.rationale: A motor converts electrical energy into mechanical motion.

questions.text: Which law states that the induced emf is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux?
questions.rationale: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction.

questions.text: Which device is used to measure electric current?
questions.rationale: An ammeter measures electric current.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux?
questions.rationale: Magnetic flux is measured in webers (Wb).

questions.text: Which law relates the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor?
questions.rationale: Ampere's law relates current to the magnetic field.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
questions.rationale: Electric charge is measured in coulombs (C).

questions.text: Which device stores electric charge?
questions.rationale: A capacitor stores electric charge.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of capacitance?
questions.rationale: Capacitance is measured in farads (F).

questions.text: Like charges ___ each other.
questions.rationale: Like charges repel; opposite charges attract.

questions.text: Which is a characteristic of a democratic leader?
questions.rationale: Democratic leaders involve the team in decisions.

questions.text: Which is a method of staff motivation?
questions.rationale: Recognition and rewards motivate staff.

questions.text: Which is a key component of patient safety?
questions.rationale: Medication safety and fall prevention are key.

questions.text: Which is a method of effective communication in healthcare?
questions.rationale: SBAR is an effective communication tool.

questions.text: Which is a key component of nursing documentation?
questions.rationale: Accurate and complete documentation is essential.

questions.text: Which is a method of staff development?
questions.rationale: Continuing education develops staff.

questions.text: Which is a key component of infection control management?
questions.rationale: Standard precautions prevent infection.

questions.text: Which is a method of resource management in nursing?
questions.rationale: Efficient use of supplies is resource management.

questions.text: Which is a key component of a nursing care plan?
questions.rationale: Care plans include goals and interventions.

questions.text: Which is a method of evaluating nursing care?
questions.rationale: Patient outcomes and audits evaluate care.

questions.text: Which is a common symptom of bipolar disorder?

options.label: A
options.text: Mood swings between mania and depression

questions.correctText: Mood swings between mania and depression
questions.rationale: Bipolar disorder involves mood swings between mania and depression.

questions.text: Which is a common symptom of obsessive-compulsive disorder?
questions.rationale: OCD involves repetitive thoughts and behaviors.

questions.text: Which is a therapeutic communication technique?
questions.rationale: Active listening is a therapeutic technique.

questions.text: Which is a common symptom of post-traumatic stress disorder?
questions.rationale: Flashbacks are a symptom of PTSD.

questions.text: Which is a priority nursing intervention for a patient with acute psychosis?
questions.rationale: Safety and antipsychotics are priority for acute psychosis.

questions.text: Which is a common symptom of dementia?
questions.rationale: Memory loss is a hallmark of dementia.
